h1:
Things to Do in Nong Khai
The Mekong, Temples & Nature Worth the Trip
intro: Nong Khai is a Mekong town you can wander slowly all day without getting bored. Wake up early and walk the riverfront watching the sun rise over Laos, spend the afternoon among the strange sculptures at Sala Kaew Ku, pay your respects to Luang Pho Phra Sai at Wat Pho Chai, then come back in the evening to catch the breeze along the riverside road. With a bit more time you can drive out to quiet temples by the water and a clifftop skywalk. We've gathered the places actually worth your time here — a mix of riverfront, culture and nature, with up-to-date entry fees and opening hours so you can plan straight away.

blocks.html: What makes Nong Khai special is that everything plays off the Mekong River. In town there's a long riverside walkway, an old waterfront market, and sacred temples the whole province holds dear. The big draw known across Thailand is Sala Kaew Ku, a huge concrete sculpture garden you won't find anywhere else. If you want to head further out, there are quiet riverside temples and a clifftop viewpoint reached by driving along the Mekong road. We've split everything into three groups so it's easy to picture: the riverfront in town, the culture and merit-making spots, and the nature and clifftop views outside town.

blocks.text: The riverfront in town — walkable all day

blocks.html: Where travelers spend the most time is the Mekong riverfront in the middle of town. The old market, the waterside walkway and the naga photo spots are all within walking distance of each other here — no driving needed. You can stroll the whole thing comfortably from afternoon into the evening.

items.name: Tha Sadet Market (Indochina Market)
items.blurb: An old riverfront market in the center of town selling dried goods, Vietnamese food, products from Laos and across Indochina, clothes and souvenirs all in one place. It's fun to wander and photograph. Open daily roughly 8am–6pm, and a good starting point for a riverside walk.

items.name: Riverside road + Naga plaza
items.blurb: A walkway running the whole length of town along the Mekong, with viewpoints over the Laos side and naga statues for photos. The evening breeze is lovely — locals come out to exercise and sit in the cool air. It's the best spot in town to watch the sunset.

items.name: Nong Khai Walking Street
items.blurb: A riverside walking street behind Tha Sadet Market, open only Saturday evenings roughly 4pm–10pm, with local food, sweets, souvenirs and performances and a river view the whole way. A great evening for eating and wandering.

blocks.title: Tip for the riverside walk
blocks.html: The hour before sunset is when the riverfront looks best — the sky shifts colors over Laos, the sun is gentle, and it's easy walking. If you come on a Saturday, leave time to roll straight into the walking street in the evening, since it's in the same spot.

items.label: Day trips from Nong Khai
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.ctaLabel: 🎟️ See all Nong Khai tours & activities (Klook)

blocks.html: Nong Khai is a town deeply tied to beliefs around the naga and sacred Buddha images. So this group includes both temples where people genuinely come to make wishes, and Sala Kaew Ku, a huge belief-driven sculpture work you can't see anywhere else. You can fit several of these into a single day since they're in and around town.

items.name: Sala Kaew Ku (Sculpture Park)
items.blurb: An open-air museum with over 200 large concrete sculptures — Buddha images, bodhisattvas, Hindu gods, Ramakien characters and scenes from folk belief. The tallest stands several dozen meters high, and you can easily spend an hour walking through it. It's the place most people picture first when they think of Nong Khai.
items.meta: Open 8am–6pm · Wat That subdistrict, ~3 km from town

items.name: Wat Pho Chai (Luang Pho Phra Sai)
items.blurb: A royal temple in the center of town on Prajak Road, home to Luang Pho Phra Sai, the city's revered Buddha image that locals hold in deep respect. People stop by to pray all day long. It's right in town, just a few minutes' walk or drive from the riverfront. Free entry.

items.name: Wat Phra That Bang Phuan
items.blurb: An ancient stupa dating to the Lan Xang era, with a square-based chedi. What draws the crowds is the sacred well and the Naga Muchalinda statue, believed to grant wishes. Merit-makers shouldn't skip it. It's about 23 km outside town — an easy enough drive.

items.name: First Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge
items.blurb: The bridge across the Mekong linking Nong Khai with Vientiane, looking great from the riverfront in town. It's both a photo spot and the border crossing for a day trip into Laos. If you want to extend your trip to Vientiane, you start here.
items.meta: Visible from the riverfront daily · border crossing

items.name: Nong Khai Aquarium
items.blurb: An aquarium at Khon Kaen University's Nong Khai campus showing Mekong-basin freshwater fish and sea fish, with a glass tunnel where fish swim around you. Good for kids and for getting out of the sun. It's south of town.

blocks.title: An honest word about Sala Kaew Ku
blocks.html: Sala Kaew Ku is a very unusual belief-driven sculpture work. Some people love it for being strange and fun to photograph; others find it a little eerie, since there are so many statues and some look unsettling. Going late morning to early afternoon when the light is bright makes for an easier walk than near closing time, and there's little shade — bring water and a hat.

blocks.text: Nature and riverside temples outside town

blocks.html: If you have a car and another half-day to full day, drive along the Mekong out of town toward Si Chiang Mai and Sangkhom districts. You'll find quiet, scenic riverside temples and a clifftop skywalk that looks out over the whole curve of the Mekong. This route still isn't fully on the tourist map — good for anyone who likes nature and quiet.

items.name: Wat Pha Tak Suea + Skywalk
items.blurb: A mountainside temple in Sangkhom district with a U-shaped clear-glass skywalk jutting out from the cliff — Thailand's first skywalk. Look down and you see the curve of the Mekong and the Laos side stretching out; early mornings you may catch a sea of mist. The temple provides shoes to change into, there's no entry fee (a donation box only), and it's about 90 km from town.

items.name: Wat Hin Mak Peng
items.blurb: A riverside meditation center of Luang Pu Thet Thetrangsi in Si Chiang Mai district — shady, calm and quiet, with three boulders by the water that give the place its name. The Mekong view is gorgeous and it's a fine spot to sit quietly. Open 8:30am–4:30pm, about 75 km from town.

blocks.title: Allow extra time for the distances
blocks.html: Wat Pha Tak Suea and Wat Hin Mak Peng are in a different direction from the in-town temples, and fairly far out. The riverside road is beautiful but winding, so allow extra driving time. If you want the skywalk with a sea of mist you'll need to leave before dawn — don't cram it into the same day as the in-town sights too tightly.

On the way back, stop at Wat Phra That Bang Phuan to make a wish to the naga

items.note: An easy-paced trip leaves energy for an evening stroll

items: One day — focus on town: Wat Pho Chai, Sala Kaew Ku and Tha Sadet Market, then finish on the riverfront at sunset. Easy to cover in a single day.
Two days — first day in town and on the riverfront, second day drive out to the Wat Pha Tak Suea skywalk, Wat Hin Mak Peng, and Wat Phra That Bang Phuan on the way back.
Getting around — in town, a private car or rented motorbike is easiest, and the close spots are within walking distance of each other. For the temples outside town you'll need a vehicle.
What to wear — cover shoulders and knees for temples, and bring a hat and water; the riverfront and Sala Kaew Ku have little shade, and the midday sun is strong.

faq.q: Is one day enough in Nong Khai?
faq.a: Yes, if you focus on the in-town sights that are close together — paying respects to Luang Pho Phra Sai at Wat Pho Chai, walking among the sculptures at Sala Kaew Ku, wandering Tha Sadet Market, and finishing by the river in the evening. You can fit it all in one day. The skywalk and the riverside temples outside town are best saved for a second day.

faq.q: How much is entry to Sala Kaew Ku and what are the hours?
faq.a: Sala Kaew Ku is open daily 8am–6pm. Entry is ฿20 for Thai adults, ฿10 for children, and ฿40 for foreigners. It's in Wat That subdistrict, about 3 km from town, and you can spend roughly 1–2 hours walking through the sculptures.

faq.q: Is the Wat Pha Tak Suea skywalk far from town?
faq.a: It's fairly far — in Sangkhom district, about 90 km from Nong Khai town, roughly an hour and a half driving along the Mekong. The skywalk has no entry fee, just a donation box, and if you want to catch a sea of mist you'll need to leave before dawn.

faq.q: What merit-making spots does Nong Khai have?
faq.a: The main ones are Wat Pho Chai in town, home to Luang Pho Phra Sai, and Wat Phra That Bang Phuan about 23 km outside town, where people make wishes to the Naga Muchalinda in the sacred well. Both are free to enter and are deeply revered by locals and merit-makers alike.

faq.q: What days is Nong Khai Walking Street open?
faq.a: The riverside walking street behind Tha Sadet Market is open only on Saturday evenings, roughly 4pm–10pm, with local food, souvenirs and performances and a Mekong view the whole way. If you come on a weekday you can still walk the riverfront and Tha Sadet Market as usual.
